title: LATERAL JOIN (Correlated Subqueries in FROM)
description: Execute subqueries and set-returning functions for each row of the preceding table using PostgreSQL's powerful LATERAL keyword.

data.text: In standard SQL, subqueries inside the `FROM` clause cannot reference columns from preceding tables in the same `FROM` list. PostgreSQL's **`LATERAL`** keyword unlocks this capability, acting like a `foreach` loop that executes the inner subquery for every single row of the outer table.
Top-N Rows Per Category with LATERAL

A classic SQL challenge is fetching the top 3 most recent articles for every department or category. Traditional window functions require scanning the entire table first. A `LATERAL` join performs an index seek per category, making it orders of magnitude faster on large datasets.

data.title: Top 3 Products Per Category via LATERAL JOIN
data.content: The inner query references c.id from the outer categories table.
data.code:
SELECT 
    c.id AS category_id,
    c.name AS category_name,
    top_products.id AS product_id,
    top_products.title,
    top_products.sales_count
FROM categories c
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT p.id, p.title, p.sales_count
    FROM products p
    WHERE p.category_id = c.id
    ORDER BY p.sales_count DESC
    LIMIT 3
) top_products ON true;

data.text: LATERAL is not limited to correlated subqueries. It can also call a set-returning function per row, which is how you explode an array or generate a fixed number of rows for each parent. The pattern below expands each order into one row per line item stored as a JSON array.

data.title: Exploding an array per row with LATERAL
data.content: `jsonb_array_elements` returns one row per array element, and LATERAL lets it see `o.lines` from the current order row.
data.code:
SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    item->>'sku'                 AS sku,
    (item->>'qty')::int          AS qty,
    (item->>'price')::numeric    AS price
FROM orders AS o
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(o.lines) AS item
WHERE o.status = 'COMPLETED'
ORDER BY o.id, sku;

data.title: LATERAL vs window functions
data.text: For 'top N per group', both approaches are valid. A window function (`ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ...)`) scans the table once and sorts. LATERAL runs the inner query per outer row, which is faster when each group is small and the inner query can use an index, and slower when the outer set is large. Compare the two plans with `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` rather than assuming.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `LATERAL` allows subqueries in the `FROM` clause to reference columns from preceding tables.
Solves the 'Top-N per group' problem with optimal index seek performance.
Can be paired with `LEFT JOIN ... ON true` to preserve outer records with zero subquery matches.
